promise: You stop trusting Incognito to hide you from your boss, school or Wi-Fi.
audience_pain: People open Incognito at work or school to feel hidden.

options.line: Incognito mode makes me invisible online, right?
Incognito does not make you invisible.

hook.why: A confident wrong belief said as a question: the viewer needs the correction.

beats.job: Zoe contradicts him with who can still see
Zoe says what it really does, with the real Chrome Help page on screen
Dan realises the stakes (fear) and Zoe lands the dry answer
Zoe asks for the keyword and loops back to incognito

retention.device: jolt: close-up on Dan plus a giant WHAT?! impact word and a boom
cut from 3D to the real Chrome Help page, highlighted, over a blurred real photo
slow push-in on the fear face

overlay_plan.device: plaque (headline banner like the reference) INCOGNITO = INVISIBLE?
overlay_plan.why: the reference uses a yellow banner; ours changes text as the claim flips
names who can still see, which the voice only lists
a source on screen for the claim

share.reason: People send it to a colleague who "goes incognito" at work.

reference.twist: Same two-person comic argument, but 3-second shots, a real Chrome Help proof card, event-tied sound, and a last line that loops to the hook.
